svg.title: Estimated VCCIN current against the 570A figure ASUS quotes for the Dominus Extreme
svg.desc: Five horizontal bars show estimated total VCCIN current for a W-3175X: about 177 amps at stock, 222 amps at an illustrative 400 watts, 213 amps for my rig at 400 watts and a measured 1.876 volts, 356 amps at a 4.6 GHz overclock, and 417 amps at a 4.6 GHz AVX overclock, against the 570 amp figure ASUS quotes, marked as a dashed red line. These are estimates, not measured currents.
svg.text: Estimated VCCIN current vs. the 570A figure ASUS quotes
Estimates — CPU power ÷ VCCIN, shared equally across 32 stages. Not measured currents.
My rig — Cinebench, ~400 W (HWiNFO) @ 1.876 V (measured at the VIN pad)
4.6 GHz overclock, AVX load — ~792 W @ ~1.9 V
Power figures: Tom's Hardware W-3175X review and overclocking article (their method isn't verified here). Stages: 32× IR3555, 60A each.
570A+ is the figure ASUS quotes under Cooling → Active Heatsink — a manufacturer reference, not a standalone VRM rating.
Voltages are assumptions, except my rig's 1.876 V (measured). Assumes all CPU power flows through VCCIN; real values will differ.
